html:
The Berber Spring was a wave of protests and strikes in Kabylia and Algiers in March and April 1980, after the authorities banned a lecture on old Kabyle poetry by the writer Mouloud Mammeri at the university of Tizi Ouzou.

Since independence the state had pushed Arabic as the only national language and treated Berber identity as a threat to unity. Students occupied the university, and the police broke the protests up by force.

It was the first open challenge to the single-party state. The movement went on, through the deadly protests of the Black Spring in 2001. Tamazight, the Berber language, became a national language in 2002 and an official one in 2016, written in Tifinagh or Latin letters. See also Algeria.
sum: The Berber Spring was a wave of protests and strikes in Kabylia and Algiers in March and April 1980, after the authorities banned a lecture on old Kabyle poetry by the writer Mouloud Mammeri at the university of Tizi Ouzou.
